newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, market to recover.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, market to recover.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on higher turnover on Tuesday, and analysts said trade could get brisker with big buyers reversing the downward trend that marked the past weeks.
A trader at Metroholding brokerage said Tuesday's trading in food processor Podravka, with a big investor buying large packages, led to a small revolution at the market.
"This created some kind of security...Small investors are timid, and they always wait for a signal from big buyers. They just need to be encouraged," he said.
He also said fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka and drugs firm Pliva would not be affected by the general trend, but would rather follow developments in London.
Of seven active issues that traded, four rose and three fell. Turnover rose to 15 million kuna, up from Friday's meagre 2.1 million. Volume was also eight times higher at 17,578.
Most active Zagrebacka Banka sold 10,517 shares. It rose 35 kuna to 1,025. The bank's E-series was the top gainer, climbing 70 kuna to 430, on volume of 743 shares.
Pliva jumped 399 kuna to 13,200, selling 195 units. Boosted by a rise in the dollar, traders saw its price in Zagreb going up to catch up with its GDRs in London.
Pliva has repurchased 40,000 of its GDRs in London, at $49.25 per item, as part of plans to repurchase up to five percent of its stock. On Tuesday its GDRs traded at $49,875.
Podravka added five kuna to 220 on volume of 5,568 shares.
Biggest decliner hotelier Jadranturist lost 45 kuna to 220, with 60 shares sold. Another hotelier Laguna Porec edged down 30 kuna to 950, with 100 shares changing hands.
Confectioner Kras, down 10 kuna to 390, sold 395 shares.
